name: Barbell Overhead Press (Military Press)
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at upper-chest height and grip it just outside shoulder width with knuckles facing up.
Unrack the bar so it rests on your front delts, brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and stand with feet about hip-width apart.
Tuck your chin slightly and press the bar straight up, moving your head back out of the path as the bar passes your face.
Lock out with the bar stacked over your mid-foot and ears, pushing your head 'through' the window so your biceps finish near your ears.
Lower the bar under control back to the front of your shoulders and reset before the next rep.
formCues: Keep your core braced and ribs down to avoid leaning back
Squeeze your glutes to protect the lower back
Drive the bar in a straight vertical line over mid-foot
commonMistakes: Excessive lower-back arch from flaring the ribs up and leaning backward
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up
Letting the bar drift away from the face on the way up

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with an upright back support and rest a dumbbell on each thigh.
Kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height so they sit just outside your shoulders, palms facing forward.
Brace your core and press both dumbbells up and slightly inward until your arms are nearly straight overhead.
Pause briefly at the top without locking out aggressively or clanking the weights together.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to shoulder level and repeat.
formCues: Keep wrists stacked over elbows throughout
Press up and slightly in, not straight out wide
Keep your back against the pad and avoid arching
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back off the bench to push heavier weight
Letting the elbows drift too far behind the body at the bottom
Using momentum or a partial range of motion

name: Seated Arnold Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing toward you with elbows in front of your chest.
Brace your core, then press up while rotating your palms outward so they face forward as the dumbbells rise.
Continue pressing until your arms are nearly extended overhead with palms facing away from you.
Reverse the motion smoothly, rotating your palms back toward your face as you lower to the start.
Control the descent fully before beginning the next rep.
formCues: Rotate the wrists smoothly and continuously with the press
Keep the tempo controlled, not jerky
Keep your core braced and back against the pad
commonMistakes: Rotating the wrists too fast or out of sync with the press
Using excessive weight that breaks form and strains the shoulder
Flaring the elbows aggressively and stressing the rotator cuff

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in, with a slight bend in the elbows.
Brace your core, keep a tall chest, and soften your knees.
Raise both dumbbells out to the sides, leading with your elbows, until your arms reach about shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top with your wrists no higher than your elbows, then lower under control.
Resist the weight all the way down before starting the next rep.
formCues: Lead with the elbows, keeping a fixed soft bend
Stop at shoulder height and don't shrug past it
Control the lowering phase with no swinging
commonMistakes: Using momentum and swinging the torso to lift the weight
Shrugging the traps and raising the arms above shoulder level
Going too heavy and turning it into an upright-row motion

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand resting in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Brace your core, keep a tall posture, and hold a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise one or both dumbbells straight in front of you until your arms reach about shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, keeping the movement smooth and controlled.
Lower the dumbbells back to your thighs under control and repeat.
formCues: Keep the elbows slightly bent and fixed
Raise only to shoulder height, no higher
Avoid leaning back to heave the weight up
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso and using momentum
Lifting the dumbbells well above shoulder height
Shrugging the shoulders at the top of the rep

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, keeping your back flat.
Let the dumbbells hang beneath your shoulders with palms facing each other and a slight bend in the elbows.
Brace your core, then raise the dumbbells out to the sides by squeezing your shoulder blades and rear delts.
Lift until your arms are roughly in line with your torso, leading with the elbows.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to the start and repeat without rounding the back.
formCues: Keep a flat back and braced core throughout the hinge
Lead with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades
Use a light weight and focus on the rear delt contraction
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back during the hinge
Using too much weight and turning it into a row with the traps
Jerking the weights up with momentum instead of controlled raises

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and stand side-on to the machine, gripping the handle with the hand farthest from the stack.
Let the working arm cross slightly in front of your body with a soft bend in the elbow, and brace your core.
Raise your arm out to the side, leading with the elbow, until it reaches about shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, keeping tension on the lateral delt, then lower under control against the cable.
Finish all reps, then turn around and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Lead with the elbow and keep the bend fixed
Let the cable pull the arm down slowly for constant tension
Stay tall and avoid leaning away from the stack
commonMistakes: Leaning hard away from the machine to swing the weight up
Shrugging the trap and raising the arm above shoulder height
Letting the weight stack slam down between reps

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core, lift your chest, and set your shoulders down to start.
Pull the dumbbells straight up close to your body by raising your elbows out and up.
Stop when your upper arms reach about shoulder height, keeping your elbows level with or slightly below your wrists.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to your thighs and repeat.
formCues: Lead with the elbows and keep the weights close to the body
Do not raise the elbows above shoulder height, to protect the shoulder joint
Keep your wrists relaxed and at or below elbow level
commonMistakes: Pulling the elbows up too high, risking shoulder impingement
Using a stance that is too narrow and overloading the wrists
Heaving with the lower back instead of a controlled pull
